fields.meta_description: Build a tournament registration form that takes entry fees and puts each team or pair in its division, with every entry in a table you own.
fields.h1: Build a Tournament Registration Form That Fills Your Bracket
fields.hero_description: Describe your event and its divisions. Emergent builds the tournament registration form with entry fees and waivers, and keeps every entry in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Tournament Entry Needs to Capture
fields.features_subheading: An entry is more than a name and an email. These six pieces turn sign-ups into a draw you can run on the day.
fields.feature_1:
One form for players and teams

Ask whether someone is entering alone or with others, and the form changes to fit. A captain adds every player on one screen, and the whole roster lands in a single entry.
fields.feature_2:
Divisions that close when full

Set a cap for each division, such as 24 pairs in 3.5 doubles. Once a division fills, its option turns into a waitlist while the other divisions stay open for new entries.
fields.feature_3:
Entry fees per team or per player

Collect a flat team fee through Stripe or split it between players, with an early-bird price that ends on a date you pick. Every payment is attached to its entry in the database.
fields.feature_4:
Waivers signed during sign-up

Show your waiver text before the payment step and capture each player's signature. Parents sign for anyone under 18, and the director sees which entries still lack a signed waiver.
fields.feature_5:
Entries sorted and ready to seed

Every entry sits in one table with its division and payment status. Sort it by rating to seed the draw, then download a CSV for your bracket software or ask Emergent to build it.
fields.feature_6:
The club's domain, the club's code

Publish the form on the club's own domain and keep the source in GitHub. A volunteer developer can add a live scoreboard or a results page later without touching registration.

fields.usecase_heading: Registration for Every Kind of Tournament
fields.tab_content_1:
Foursomes go into a flight on their combined handicap

Each golfer in the foursome enters a Handicap Index when the captain registers for the Lakeview Rotary scramble. The form adds up the team's numbers. Teams under 60 combined go to Flight A. The rest play in Flight B. Nobody sorts the pairings sheet by hand the night before.
fields.tab_content_2:
No U12 schedule until every birth year checks out

Coaches type in the roster with birth dates to enter the Fox Valley Spring Cup. The director sets 2015 as the U12 birth year, and the form checks each player against it. One player born in 2014 holds the Hawks' roster, and the coach gets an email naming the player before the 16-team schedule is built.
fields.tab_content_3:
Teams that miss check-in lose their seat

Thirty minutes before the first match, every captain in the 32-team bracket gets a check-in link by email. A captain taps it to confirm all five players are online. When the window closes, an unconfirmed seat goes to the first team on the waitlist, and the bracket admins see the swap in their channel.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each partner pays half before the pair is drawn

One player registers the pair for 3.5 doubles at the Sunbelt Paddle Club Fall Classic and pays $35, half of the $70 team entry. The partner gets an email to confirm and pay the rest. Only when both halves clear does the pair go into the 3.5 draw, and a pair still unpaid after 48 hours loses the spot.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Tournament Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Work back from the draw. Every question should help you seed a team or reach a captain on the day.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the format first: single elimination, round robin, pool play into a bracket, or a scramble. It tells you whether an entry is one person, a pair or a full roster, and how many entries one day of play can hold.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List each division with its cap and the rule that decides who belongs there, whether that is an age cutoff, a skill rating or a combined handicap. Each rule becomes a question on the form and a check that runs on submit.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what makes an entry complete. For most events it means paid with a signed waiver, and in doubles both partners must have paid and signed. Entries missing either stay pending, and pending entries never reach the draw.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write a prompt with your divisions and eligibility rules, and paste the waiver word for word. Emergent builds the form with its payment step, along with the table where entries land. Change any of it later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose when an unpaid or unconfirmed entry gets a reminder and when it gives up its spot, for example 48 hours for a partner to pay. Waitlisted captains should hear by email the moment a spot opens up.
fields.howto_step_6_des: For events with a fixed start, send a check-in link before the first match and decide what happens to no-shows. Releasing their seat to the waitlist keeps the bracket full without anyone working the phones at the venue.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it as a made-up team
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form as a made-up team that breaks a rule, such as a player too old for the division or a partner who never pays. Confirm the entry stays pending and the right person hears about it. Then share the link.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (Jotform, Fluent Forms, FormNX, Typeform's gaming template, pdfFiller), a SportsEngine help article and one club's soccer PDF. None of them deal with what makes a tournament different from other sign-ups: entries that come in as teams or pairs, divisions with their own caps and eligibility rules, ratings that decide where a team plays, and entries that only count once fees and check-in are done. This page is for the tournament director who has to turn registrations into a draw, with golf flights, soccer rosters, gaming check-in and doubles partners as the four cases.
tab_stories: A charity golf scramble adds up each foursome's four Handicap Index numbers and puts teams under 60 combined in Flight A and everyone else in Flight B.
A club soccer tournament checks every player's birth year on a U12 roster against the division's cutoff and sends the coach the one name that fails before the schedule is built.
A 32-team online gaming bracket sends each captain a check-in link 30 minutes before the start and gives any seat that stays empty to the first team on the waitlist.
A pickleball doubles tournament lets one player register a pair, emails the partner to confirm and pay their half of the $70 entry, and places the pair in the 3.5 draw only when both halves are paid.
